header.title: Open BIM Studio
header.heroAlt: Open BIM Studio: 3D view of a concrete pavilion with a section box cutting away the roof, revealing columns, walls and floor
header.label: BIM modelling
header.tagline: From first layout to reinforcement and drawings, in one open BIM model
header.desc: Set out levels, grids, walls and floors, then develop the same model with reinforcement, connections, sections and sheets. Everything stays in IFCX, the open OpenAEC format.

meta.description: Free, open-source BIM modeller in development: walls, floors and grids, reinforcement, connections, plans, sections and sheets from one model, saved as IFCX. Preview for Linux.
meta.title: Open BIM Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

model.alt: Structural plan of an example building with grids, layered walls and the ribbon with tools for walls, floors, roofs and columns
model.title: Set out a building the way you sketch
model.desc: Levels, grids, layered walls, floors, roofs, columns, beams and piles sit in one ribbon. Grab a grip, snap to the grid and push or pull a face to the right size.

rebar.alt: Plan of a concrete pavilion with reinforcement meshes, cages and position labels, and the Reinforcement ribbon with bar, L bar, U bar, cage, mesh and area
rebar.title: Reinforcement that follows the concrete
rebar.desc: Place bars, stirrup cages, meshes and area reinforcement parametrically in beams, columns and slabs. Position labels with diameter and spacing appear on the drawing in Dutch or international notation.

view3d.alt: 3D wireframe of the pavilion inside a section box, with the reinforcement in slab, columns, walls and pad foundations visible
view3d.title: Look straight through the model
view3d.desc: Cut the model open with a section box and orbit it with the view cube. The wireframe shows the reinforcement in slabs, columns and pad foundations; shadows, colour and hidden lines switch on or off with one click.

sheets.alt: Sheet A-201 on A2 with two sections of the pavilion at 1:50, level markers, a legend and a title block, next to the project browser with sheets
sheets.title: Sheets that move with the model
sheets.desc: Plans, sections and elevations come straight from the model, with dimensions, tags and drawing standards. Place them on a sheet with a title block and export to PDF or SVG.

notice.text: Development preview for Linux: not yet ready for real projects. Work on copies of your files. Testers wanted.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Model, reinforce and draw in one model
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

levels.title: Levels and grids
levels.desc: Work per level with PgUp and PgDn, and repeat grid lines with a pattern such as 5000 3x5400.

walls.title: Walls, floors and roofs
walls.desc: Layered walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, skirtings and spaces.

structure.title: Columns, beams and piles
structure.desc: Structural members in concrete or steel, with a library of European steel sections.

openings.title: Windows, doors and window systems
openings.desc: Openings, Dutch doors and your own types, and window systems hosted in the wall.

direct.title: Push, pull and snap
direct.desc: Grips, numeric input, snapping to end, mid and intersection points, Push/Pull and face splitting.

systems.title: Parametric building systems
systems.desc: System types with frames and panels, stairs, railings and component libraries.

bars.title: Bars, cages and meshes
bars.desc: Straight, L and U bars, stirrup cages, meshes and area reinforcement, parametric in the host.

notation.title: Positions and notation
notation.desc: Position labels with count, diameter and spacing, in Dutch or international notation.

rebarview.title: Light display in 3D
rebarview.desc: Reinforcement as centre lines for a smooth view; switch on the real diameter when you need it.

connections.title: Steel connections
connections.desc: Parametric joints with plates, bolts, welds and member cuts, as reusable types.

plans.title: Plans and sections
plans.desc: Views with their own scale, cut height, hatching and drawing type, straight from the model.

sheets.title: Sheets to PDF and SVG
sheets.desc: Place views on a sheet with paper size, title block and legend, and output it as PDF or SVG.

schedules.title: Schedules and quantities
schedules.desc: Schedules of walls, windows and doors, floors, spaces and reinforcement, with length, area and volume, exportable as CSV.

sectionbox.title: 3D with section box
sectionbox.desc: Shaded, hidden line or wireframe, with shadows, a view cube and a section box you move with grips.

ifcx.title: IFCX as the project file
ifcx.desc: Your work is stored as compact binary IFCX (.ifcxb) or JSON IFCX, readable by the other OpenAEC apps.

ifc.title: IFC in and out
ifc.desc: Import and export IFC; supported elements become editable objects, the rest stays as reference.

dxf.title: DXF as underlay
dxf.desc: Read a DXF drawing as reference geometry to model over.

mcp.title: AI assistant via MCP
mcp.desc: A local API and an MCP adapter let scripts and AI assistants create walls, floors and grids and change properties.

explorer.title: Model explorer
explorer.desc: Levels, grids, types and views in a tree, with the properties alongside.

undo.title: Undo and redo
undo.desc: Every edit is one step you can undo or redo.

download.title: Download v0.1.1
download.lead: Free, no account needed. Preview for Linux x86-64 with Vulkan; a tested Windows version is not available yet.
download.metaLinux: .run installer for Linux x86-64, per user
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open BIM Studio is a desktop app. Download it on your computer.

sectionbox.title: Section box
sectionbox.desc: Cut the 3D model open with grips and look inside.

rebar.title: Reinforcement in the model
rebar.desc: Cages, bars and meshes are now part of the main app, with a light centre-line display.

sketch.title: Sketch editing
sketch.desc: Edit sketch lines and faces before they become building elements.

props.title: Views and properties
props.desc: Scale, cut height, hatching and drawing type per view in the properties panel.

exchange.title: IFC and DXF
exchange.desc: Improved import and export of IFC and DXF underlays.

installer.title: Installer with menu entry
installer.desc: One file installs per user, without admin rights, and replaces an older version.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.1.1
whatsnew.title: First Linux preview, more in one app
whatsnew.desc: Version 0.1.1 bundles the work since the first preview into one Linux installer: modelling, reinforcement, section box, properties, sketching and IFC/DXF.

files.a: Projects in binary IFCX (.ifcxb) or JSON IFCX (.ifcx), IFC files from other BIM software and DXF drawings as underlay. Not every imported IFC object becomes fully editable; keep your source files.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Yes. There is no web version. Download the Linux installer (.run) and start it with bash; it installs per user in your home folder and adds the app to the menu.

cost.a: Nothing. Open BIM Studio is open source under the MPL-2.0 licence, with no account or subscription.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: In IFCX, the open OpenAEC format: compact binary as .ifcxb or as JSON (.ifcx). You can also export to IFC, drawings to PDF or SVG and schedules to CSV. The format is still evolving; work on copies.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: On Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38 or newer, an X11 session (or XWayland) and a graphics card with Vulkan. A tested Windows installer is not available yet; macOS not yet either.

practice.a: It works with levels, grids, IFC and Dutch reinforcement notation, and has European steel sections. It is a preview: there is no IFC certification and no check against building codes.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: Through the MCP adapter or the local API, an assistant creates walls, floors, grids and building systems, selects elements, changes properties and types, and undoes steps.

ready.q: Can I use it for a real project yet?
ready.a: Not yet. It is a development preview: not every combination of features is finished or tested, and performance on large models is still being improved. Try it with the example building and report what you find.

dynlex.a: The programming language the modeller is written in, developed within OpenAEC. The code reads almost like English and is compiled to fast native code via LLVM.

language.q: What language is the interface in?
language.a: In English for now. Country-specific content, such as Dutch reinforcement notation, is chosen per project.

dynlex.desc: The BIM logic, tools and geometry are written in DynLex and compiled to native code via LLVM.

kernel.title: Own CAD kernel
kernel.desc: Planar geometry, NURBS and B-rep in its own kernel; the model keeps the objects, a separate layer derives the geometry.

vulkan.title: Vulkan and GLFW
vulkan.desc: A native interface that talks to the graphics card directly, with no browser or runtime in between.

ifcx.desc: The open data format of the OpenAEC ecosystem, binary (.ifcxb) or JSON, alongside IFC for exchange.

mcp.desc: A stdio MCP server and a local HTTP API drive the editor; every model edit is one undo step.

license.desc: The app source code is under MPL-2.0; the DynLex runtime under LGPL-3.0. Releases come with SHA256 sums and a signature.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
